summary: A set stores each item once and checks membership in O(1) on average by using hash values. Your own class needs both __eq__ and __hash__ for a set to treat equal objects as duplicates.
notes: __hash__ returns hash(self.student_id) because it uses the same field as __eq__. Equal objects must have equal hashes.
Without either method, Python compares objects by identity, so two separate Maya objects count as two students.
attendance & club is the intersection: students in both sets.
pitfall: Defining __eq__ without __hash__ sets __hash__ to None, and adding the object to a set raises TypeError: unhashable type.
